structural_coordinates: Parabolic scaling separates time-integrated first-derivative control from a uniform time-slice derivative norm.

AB finite-I controls velocity A/C, pressure D, and spacetime gradient E on parabolic cylinders; the source theorem does not list a uniform time-slice vorticity Lorentz norm or normalized-direction BMO norm as an output.
Grujic v2 consumes global uniform-in-time critical vorticity amplitude and global logarithmic BMO direction information.
Strong local L^3 convergence of velocity does not authorize differentiation to strong vorticity convergence.
Global Lorentz/far-field gluing is a distinct obstruction from failure of a local bare functional embedding.
A divergence-free non-solution hostile near-miss may invalidate a norm-only interpolation claim while leaving PDE-specific smoothing/rigidity open.
Backward uniqueness and ancient-solution rigidity are downstream consumers; they cannot create a missing producer certificate.
Type-II classification remains outside this child.

counterexample_first_falsifier.family: A_N=(0,0,N^{-1} chi(x) cos(N x1)); v_N=curl A_N; u_N(x,t)=eta(N^2(t-t0)) v_N(x); q_N=0, with chi=1 on B_{3/4}, supp chi subset B_1, eta(0)=1 and compact time support
counterexample_first_falsifier.failure_condition: If the numerical I-signature is uniformly bounded but peak-time ||omega_N||_{L^{3/2,infinity}} and ||xi_N||_{bmo_phi} diverge, a bare bounded producer map from I-functionals to those consumer norms is refuted.
counterexample_first_falsifier.non_overreach: The family is deliberately not asserted to solve Navier-Stokes. Success does not refute NSE+finite-I -> consumer; it only blocks an interpolation/representation proof using the registered norms alone.
